title: Made of faith
hookLine: can faith without the books count? Arjuna asks, and Krishna answers
carry: a person is made of their faith
last: SHASTRA — THE TEACHING AS YOUR MEASURE.

cards: A grandmother who never read the books. She couldn't recite a single verse in Sanskrit, but she lit the lamp every evening, for as long as anyone can remember, and never once missed it. She didn't know the rules.
But she had something. Arjuna has just heard Krishna say, let scripture be your measure. His next question could be about people like her.
Chapter seventeen opens with it. What about them, Krishna? The ones who set aside the rules, but worship with faith?

teach.b: Verse one is Arjuna's question: those who set aside the rule of scripture but worship full of faith, what is their standing? Sattva, rajas or tamas? He's using the three threads from chapter fourteen.
Krishna doesn't say those people are wrong.
Verse two: faith comes in three kinds, born of each person's own nature. Then verse three. Everyone's faith takes the shape of their inner being.

teach.h: A PERSON IS MADE OF FAITH.
teach.b: A person is made of faith. Shraddhamayo 'yam purushah. Whatever their faith is, that's what they are.
Yo yac-chraddhah sa eva sah. Not: a person has a faith. A person is made of it.
The word is shraddha, often translated faith. Some teachers take it apart as shrat, truth or the heart, and dha, to place: placing your heart.
So it's less about believing a list of statements, more about where you set your trust. Then the chapter begins to sort.
Verse four: the clear-hearted worship the gods; the restless worship yakshas and rakshasas, spirits of wealth and power; the heavy worship ghosts.

Verses five and six warn about people who torture their own bodies with harsh practices the scriptures never taught, full of show and ego. They hurt the body, Krishna says, and me, who lives inside it.

So for Hindus, faith isn't a test you pass by knowing the verses. Many teachers read it this way: you become what you place your heart in, which is why a grandmother's lamp, lit every evening, matters.

how: Shraddha, faith as trust and wholehearted commitment, is a key word in Hindu practice; Gita 17.3, 'a person is made of faith', is quoted by teachers to explain why sincere practice shapes a person.

o: believing things without any proof at all
where you place your heart and your trust
a vow to keep every rule exactly right

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: faith: where you place your heart
what about faith without the rules?
a person is made of faith
no harsh show that harms the body

s: Krishna says people who don't know the rules have no real faith
he says faith comes in three kinds, born of each person's nature.
Gita 17.3 says a person is made of faith
shraddhamayo 'yam purushah: as their faith is, so are they.
the Gita praises harsh self-torture as the highest faith
verses 5–6 warn against it: it hurts the body and the divine within.

games.q: you're Arjuna. you've just heard 'let scripture be your measure.' you think of people with deep faith who never learned the rules. what do you ask?
o: should they be taught the rules first?
what is their standing: sattva, rajas or tamas?
games.why: Arjuna asks which of the three threads their faith belongs to, and Krishna answers: faith comes in three kinds, born of nature.

practice: Ask gently: where do I place my heart? Not what I say I believe, but what I actually trust, day to day: a person, a routine, money, a practice, God, my own effort.
No answer is wrong; just notice which ones rise first, and how each one feels in the body.

wordCard.voice: Shraddha, faith, trust. Gita seventeen, three: each person's faith takes the shape of their nature; a person is made of it, and as their faith is, so are they.

orig.note: Sanskrit: shraddha, faith, trust; some teachers explain it as placing (dha) the heart or truth (shrat).

carryVoice: Your line: a person is made of their faith. As your faith is, so you become. See you tomorrow.
